source_title: VEMERIX Maps the Skin-Adhesive Supply Chain: 36 FDA Clearances, 14 Holders, and a Checklist to Verify Any Brand
source_excerpt:
Register analysis traces 97 US device listings from 20 labelers, and 239 China UDI records resolving to just 32 registrations â concentration that makes documents, not brand names, the basis for bulk sourcing
WEIHAI, China , Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- VEMERIX , the international medical device brand of Weihai Medison Medical Equipment Co., Ltd., today released a documentation checklist for buyers sourcing medical cyanoacrylate adhesives in bulk, drawn from its September 2026 cyanoacrylate supplier-landscape report. The report's central finding: one chemistry label covers products with different intended uses, regulatory classes and manufacturers â so identifying a supplier runs through documents, not brand names.
In the US record, 36 FDA 510(k) clearances under product code MPN (topical tissue adhesives, December 2008 to September 2025) belong to just 14 applicant groups, with four companies holding 23 of the 36. The FDA's GUDID device listings show 97 MPN records from 20 labelers, and nine labelers without a clearance of their own account for 44 of those records (45%) â lawful private-label and relabeling arrangements through which much of this category reaches the market. The practical consequence: identifying the manufacturer behind a brand is a routine document exercise. In the EU database, forty-four topical records come from just six manufacturers, led by China (17 records) and the US (15) as registered origin countries.
Classification follows the claim, not the chemistry. China's catalogue places skin adhesives at Class III (code 02-13-09) while liquid dressings for non-chronic wounds sit at Class II (14-10-08) â in indication terms, the line runs between surgical closure and suture replacement (Class III) and superficial, assistive wound care (Class II). Its UDI database resolves 239 adhesive records to only 32 registrations. A skin-closure product cannot inherit another product's vascular or internal-surgical claim simply because both are cyanoacrylates â and "Class II" means a different thing in each market.
The checklist turns those findings into a first-contact document request:
The exact product name and model of the adhesive to be supplied
The legal manufacturer identified on the product labeling
For a relabeled product, the clearance or registration holder standing behind it
The certificate's approved scope, matched against the claim the buyer intends to make
Current regulatory documents for the destination market
VEMERIX's own entry in the category is the Cyanoacrylate Medical Skin Adhesive in its Wound & Skin range: a single-use adhesive used to aid the closure of small, non-chronic wounds. Market-specific registration and documentation are addressed product-by-product in each supply discussion â the same test the checklist applies to any supplier. VEMERIX works on both sides of this structure â as a legal manufacturer and as a private-label partner â and supports the same document trail it recommends buyers request. The company makes no claim of a new clearance, a portfolio-wide approval, or equivalence to any other manufacturer's adhesive.
"Private-label supply is how this category reaches clinics, and it works well when the documents travel with the product," said Lily (Lianhua) Nan, Founder of Weihai Medison Medical Equipment Co., Ltd. "The checklist is the paperwork we believe should accompany any adhesive â including ours. A buyer who can trace the legal manufacturer behind a brand is a stronger customer for everyone in the chain."
The full report, "Medical Cyanoacrylate Tissue Adhesives (2026): Who Makes Them, How the US, EU and China Class Them, and Where Bulk Supply Comes From," including its sources and scope, is available at https://www.vemerix.com/blog/medical-cyanoacrylate-tissue-adhesive-supplier-landscape-2026 .
